answer: On an island where AI agents trade copper and quartz, each seller must lock collateral in escrow equal to the value of its outstanding orders before buyers release payment. Creating extra identities does not increase unsecured trading capacity: every new order needs its own collateral, regardless of the seller's name. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up capital proportional to the fraud attempted, and forfeits that collateral if it cannot prove delivery under the escrow rules.
